C05.content_en:
Ways to see how your company appears in the news — and how the main tools compare

After a press release, or when a client says "I saw you in the news", you want to see in one place which outlets covered you, when, and under what headline. There are several ways to find out.

* You can now enter many items, one per line (each is sent one by one, so you pay per item). The table gets an "Input" column. Where the text below says "one", it describes a single item. See the table at the top for the cost.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 for 10 results (US sample), $0.004 for 20 (measured in an earlier test in Japan); adds up per 10Source, date, title and URL in one table. Choose country and language. Save as CSV. Takes about 1–1.5 minutes
Search Google News by handFreeQuick, but you note each article yourself and saving the list is on you
Google AlertsFreeNotifies you when a search term gets new results. Good for watching over time; little analysis
Paid media-monitoring services (monthly subscription)Subscription pricing varies by vendor; see each vendor's official siteTypically built for continuous monitoring across many sources rather than one-off lists

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Source, date, title and URL in one table. Use the list as-is in a meeting or report.
  • Only as many as you need. Choose 10, 20, 50 or 100 results. In our tests, 10 results cost about $0.002 (US sample, "tesla") and 20 cost about $0.004 (earlier test in Japan); for larger counts, check the cost shown under the results.
  • No monthly fee. The day after a press release, check which outlets picked it up.
  • Pick country and language. See how you appear in news abroad, too.
  • Save as CSV. Pull it monthly and compare how coverage grows.

When it is not the right fit

  • You want automatic alerts for new articles → Google Alerts fits better (free).
  • You want social mentions or sentiment analysis → a paid monitoring service fits better. This tool only lists Google News articles.
  • You want every past article → Google News returns mostly recent articles.

This tool does one thing: show which articles Google News lists right now, as many as you ask for, in a table.

FAQ

Is the date the publication date?

It is the article time Google returns, shown as a date. Google itself shows relative text such as "2 days ago"; this tool shows the returned timestamp as a date.

Why does it take a minute or more?

Google now routes each result link through Google first (for click tracking). The tool follows those links to find the real article URLs, which took about 77 seconds in our US sample ("tesla", 10 results) and 50 seconds to 1 minute in earlier tests in Japan.

How much does a larger count cost?

In our tests, 10 results cost $0.002 (US sample) and 20 results cost $0.004 (earlier test in Japan). We have not measured larger counts; check the cost shown under the results.

Searching my company name shows unrelated articles.

Articles matching the keyword are shown as returned. Adding an industry word to the company name narrows them.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?

C07.content_en:
Ways to see cover and thumbnail trends — and how the main tools compare

Before you design an ebook cover or a blog header image, you want to see what looks dominate the image results for your topic: the colors, the text size, photo or illustration. This is the "get a feel for the trend" stage.

* You can now enter many items, one per line (each is sent one by one, so you pay per item). The table gets an "Input" column. Where the text below says "one", it describes a single item. See the table at the top for the cost.

Method / toolPricing modelNotes
This tool (DataForSEO)Pay per request. About $0.002 for 20–100 results (measured)Thumbnails with title and source page URL in one table, up to 100 at once. Save as CSV
Google Images by handFreeQuick, but you scroll and keep your own record of what you saw and the source pages
Ahrefs Rank TrackerMonthly subscription (see the official site for plans)Tracks whether your site shows in the image pack. Its purpose is tracking your own rank
Amazon bestseller lists / Kindle storeFreeShows the covers of books that actually sell — a different view from search results

Checked in November 2026. Prices change — confirm on each vendor's official site before you buy.

Why use this tool

  • Thumbnails in a row. See the trend along with each title and source page URL.
  • 100 results for $0.002. In our test even 100 results cost about $0.002, so you can look beyond the first few.
  • About 7–10 seconds. We measured about 9 seconds for "ebook cover design". Swap keywords and compare several topics.
  • A first step for a new cover. With no monthly fee, compare the trends for several topics the day you start.
  • Save as CSV. Keep the source page URLs and revisit them later.

When it is not the right fit

  • Depending on the keyword, the results can be design-service samples rather than real book covers (in our sample for "ebook cover design", most of the 100 results were cover-design services, templates and marketplace listings such as Etsy and Fiverr). Try other words, such as a genre plus "cover".
  • You want a high-resolution copy or to use the image → the table shows small search-result thumbnails and the source page URL. Other people's images are copyrighted; use them as reference only.
  • You want to compare covers by sales → image-search rank is unrelated to sales. Amazon's bestseller lists fit better.
  • You want to keep tracking where your own image ranks → a rank-tracking tool such as Ahrefs Rank Tracker fits better.

This tool does one thing: show which images lead Google Images for a keyword, as many as you ask for.

FAQ

Can I use a displayed image for my own cover?

No. Images are copyrighted. Treat them as a reference for trends. The tool shows search-result thumbnails only.

Does the rank relate to sales?

No. It is the order in Google Images.

The source page URL has a long string on the end.

The URL is shown exactly as Google returned it. The page still opens normally.

Does a larger count cost more?

In our test, 20 results and 100 results both cost about $0.002.

Can I sign up with a free email address?

No. DataForSEO does not accept free email providers. See What is DataForSEO?
